references.text: Joshua is first mentioned as Moses' servant and military leader in the battle against Amalek.
Joshua is described as Moses' servant (משרת) who did not leave the tent, the same role as in Exodus 24:13.
Joshua, son of Nun, is identified as Moses' servant from his youth.
Joshua is appointed as Moses' successor, a role prepared through his service to Moses.
Joshua, son of Nun, who stands before Moses, will lead Israel into the land.
Joshua is described as Moses' servant (משרת), the same title used in Exodus 24:13.
The mountain of God (הר האלהים) is also mentioned as the place where Moses met God at the burning bush.
Moses goes up the mountain to meet God, the same motif found in Exodus 24:13.
The continuation of the account where Moses goes up the mountain and stays there for forty days.
Elijah travels to the mountain of God, Horeb, the same mountain Moses climbed.
Exodus 19:20 is the direct precursor and calling that Exodus 24:13 fulfills through Moses' ascent.
Joshua 11:15 confirms Joshua's role as the faithful executor of Moses' will, which gives meaning to his presence at the mountain of God in Exodus 24.
